Score as many points as possible by rolling five dice, with three rolls per round.
You may hold any dice you want after a roll, then roll the remaining dice.
Once you're happy with the roll (or you've rolled three times), score it in any open category on your scorecard.
The game ends once every category is filled.
Each *Upper Section* category, from `Ones` to `Sixes`, scores the total of the dice showing that number. For example:
Score **63pts** or more across the whole section and you earn a bonus **35pts**! That's an average of three of each number.
The *Lower Section* awards points for specific dice combinations:
Total of all five dice, if at least three dice are the same
Total of all five dice, if at least four dice are the same
Three of one number and two of another
All five dice are the same
The sum of all five dice
If you roll five matching dice, you can score a `5x` worth **50pts**.
Roll another five matching dice after already scoring a `5x`? It earns a **100pts** bonus, on top of whatever category you then score those dice in.
When you score a repeat `5x`, the Joker rule decides where it can go:
The matching *Upper Section* category, if it's still open. Five 4s must go in `Fours`, scored for **20pts**, in addition to the bonus.
Otherwise, any unscored category outside the *Upper Section*, in addition to the bonus. `Full House`, `Small Straight` and `Large Straight` score their full fixed amount.
If every category outside the *Upper Section* is already filled, you must score it in an unscored *Upper Section* category for **0pts**, but you still get the **100pts** bonus.
If multiple players end the game with the same score, the following checks are made in order. The first difference decides who wins the tie:
If all of these are equal, then it is a true tie.
A *Game Mode* changes the rules for a whole game. Choose one on the new game screen for a new way to play DiceFive.
*Standard* is the default, and plays by the rules on the *Gameplay* pages. Every other mode starts from those rules and changes some of them: more dice, different categories, etc.

Scores from *Standard*, *Tricolour* and *7 Dice Stud* go on the *Leaderboard*. The other modes' scores don't, since they can't be compared with a normal game, but every mode counts towards your *Statistics*.
Any mode can also be played with *Modifiers*, which have pages of their own.
Similar to *Standard*, but every die also rolls a colour (red, yellow or blue) alongside its number.
There are four extra scoring categories:
Three of one colour and two of another
Under the Joker rule, a repeat `5x` also scores `Coloured House` at its full **25pts**. Everything else plays exactly the same as the *Standard* rules, just with more opportunities to score.
See if you can find the Easter Egg in this mode!

A limited version of *Standard*. Every game starts with the `5x` category and **six** others, picked at random, disabled. That leaves just **six** categories to score, so a game lasts only **six** turns.
A disabled category has a slash through it. Every player in a game has the same ones disabled, and a new set is picked for each game.
With `5x` disabled, there is no Joker rule and no bonus for repeat 5x.

The *Upper Section* bonus scales based on the disabled categories. It still earns **35pts**, but the target is reduced. With `Threes` disabled you need **54pts**, which is **9pts** less. If every *Upper Section* category is disabled, there's no bonus.
The *Extended Scores* modifier's categories are never disabled.
Scores from this mode don't go on the *Leaderboard*, since every game has a different scorecard, but they still count towards your *Statistics*.
A custom mode extending the *Standard* game mode. Every roll is **seven** dice instead of five.
Like in *Standard*, you may only score with **five** held dice.
Your scorecard shows what your selection of seven dice would score, highlighting the best combination. In `4x`, these dice take the four 6s and the 5:
If multiple dice give the same highest score, the leftmost ones are chosen. Here, `Large Straight` is worth **40pts** with the 1 to 5 or the 2 to 6:
To override this, hold the dice you want first. Holding the 6 makes it the 2 to 6:
If the *Turn Timer* runs out, the first box that can still be scored is chosen.
Scoring, bonuses and the Joker rule are exactly the same as the *Standard* rules. You just get more dice to choose your hand from!
A triple variant of *Standard*. Every category is scored **three** times instead of once, so a game lasts **39** turns.
Each category can be scored up to three times, and the category is worth all of its slots added up. It stays open until all **three** are filled.
There's still just one *Upper Section* bonus, but it's tripled too: score **189pts** or more across the section to earn **105pts**.
Each of the `5x` slots takes a `5x` for **50pts**. The **100pts** bonus and the Joker rule only begin once all **three** are filled, with at least one of them scoring **50pts**.
Here's an example turn, with `Fives` already holding **15pts** and **10pts**:
The first roll lands three 5s. Hold them, and roll the other **two** dice again.
Another 5! Hold it too, and roll the last die.
The last roll is a 6. That's worth **26pts** in `4x`, or **20pts** in `Fives`.
Score it in `Fives`. It fills the last of its **three** slots, so `Fives` is closed for the rest of the game, worth **45pts** in total.
In a tie break, every slot that scored **0pts** counts as a category scored **0pts**.
Scores from this mode don't go on the *Leaderboard*, but they still count towards your *Statistics*.
Everything else plays exactly the same as the *Standard* rules, just three times over!
A custom mode with **5** dice and **3** rolls, but none of the *Standard* categories. Instead, every game deals a list of **12** targets, plus the `Alibi`.
A target names a number for the die in each place, left to right. Up to **two** places are left open, and any die fills those. This target is worth **20pts**:
Every number the target names is among your dice, in any order. Scores the target's points
Every number the target names is on the die in its own place. Scores double
At least **two** of the numbers the target names are among your dice, but not all of them. Scores half the target's points, times the share of its numbers you rolled, rounded to the nearest **5pts**

Harder targets are worth more, and each target's tile shows its points. Naming **three** numbers is worth **10pts** or **15pts**, **four** numbers **20pts** to **30pts**, and all **five** **40pts** to **75pts**. An open place makes a target easier to hit, so it's worth less.
As you roll, each target's tile has bars to show what you've successfully matched, and highlights in gold once a die is in the correct position.
Score a valid hit here instead of a matching category. It's worth the points of your best hit, but never doubled
Held dice stay where they are, so a die in the wrong place stays there until you roll it again. If nothing scores, cross off a target or the `Alibi` for **0pts**.
Here's an example turn, chasing the target above:
The first roll has the 4 and the 1 in their places, and a 2 in the open place. Hold all **three**: the 2 counts towards a hit wherever it is.
A 3 lands in its place. That's a hit for **20pts**, but the 2 is in the open place, not the fourth. Hold the 3 too.
Roll the fourth die on its own. A 2 there is an exact hit, and if it misses, the hit is safe: the last die is still a 2.
It's a 2! Score the exact hit for **40pts**. Had it missed, you could take the hit for **20pts**, or score it in the `Alibi` and keep this target for another try.
The *Extended Scores* modifier can't be used in this mode. With *Unlucky Dice*, a locked die can't count towards a target, and a roll with one locked can't be an exact hit.

Totals here don't compare with other modes, so the achievements for a high or low score, a scorecard with no zeroes, or for winning from behind after scoring three zeroes, can't be earned in it. Scores from this mode don't go on the *Leaderboard*, since every game has a different list, but they still count towards your *Statistics*.
*Modifiers* are optional extras you can add to any game mode. Choose them on the new game screen: each can be switched on or off, and some also have a value to set.
*Modifiers* are just for fun. Scores from a game with any modifier switched on don't go on the *Leaderboard*, but they still count towards your *Statistics*.

*Turn Timer* sets a limit on how long each player has to finish their turn (not each roll). Choose **30**, **60** or **120** seconds. Optionally, you may select your own value between **5**s and **999**s. The remaining time will begin to flash red when there are 5 seconds remaining.
If a player's time runs out, their roll is scored for them in whichever open category is worth the least (the first one on the scorecard, if several tie).
*Number of Rolls* sets how many times a player may roll each turn, from **1** to **9**. This overrides the default of **3** per turn.
Changing the rolls changes how easy big scores are, so with *Number of Rolls* on, certain achievements (like for a high score, a section total, etc.) can't be earned.
With *Stored Rolls*, any rolls a player doesn't use before scoring are kept for their next turn, on top of that turn's usual rolls, and so on. The dice cup shows the current total.
*Stored Rolls* can have a max configured. Leave it empty for no limit.
Extra rolls make big scores much easier, so with *Stored Rolls* on, certain achievements (like for a high score, a section total, etc.) can't be earned.
*Extended Scores* adds three more scoring categories to every player's scorecard, after the others. It works in every game mode, so the game lasts three turns longer.
Total of the four dice making two pairs of different numbers. A fifth die is never counted, even if it matches a pair
Total of the dice showing 2, 4 or 6
Total of the dice showing 1, 3 or 5

The extra categories have their own section, so they don't count towards the upper bonus or the lower section's total. With *Extended Scores* on, certain achievements (like for a high score, winning with multiple zero categories, etc.) can't be earned.

With *Unlucky Dice*, each time the dice are rolled, every die that was rolled has a chance of landing locked in a red cross of chains. A locked die can't be held and doesn't score, and a category that needs all five dice, like *5x* or the *Large Straight*, can't be scored. Dice you are holding are never locked, and a locked die can be rolled again.
Here the last **5** is locked, so it can't be held or scored. Only the other three **5**s score in *Fives*; with the locked one it would have been **20pts**. The **2** doesn't count, as usual.
You may configure the percentage chance each rolled die has of being locked, from **10%** to **50%**, and the maximum number of dice that can be locked on one roll, from **1** to **5**.
Locked dice make a bad turn easier, so with *Unlucky Dice* on, certain achievements (like for winning with multiple zero categories, etc.) can't be earned.
